title: SOC2 prep scratchpad — Kiara Reyes
content:
Quick brain dump / working notes for SOC2 scoping and control mapping. Informal — messy — actionable items at the bottom.

Context:
- Working the initial control mapping for SOC2 Type 2 (security common criteria + relevant CCs for infra and platform).
- Goal: identify gaps, assign owners, and enumerate evidence we can reasonably collect before audit window (target window Q1 2025).

High-level scope decisions (still tentative):
- In-scope systems: Redwood hosted API control plane, dedicated infra provisioning APIs, console (auth + RBAC), logging pipeline (S3/Datadog), key management integrations (KMS/HSM) as customer-facing features.
- Exclude (for now): third-party managed services we don't control (e.g., customer-owned KMS in Private deployments) — note: need scoping note for auditor.

Outstanding questions:
- Do we include Dedicated customer-managed GPUs in scope if we only provide orchestration? (Ask legal/audit: how auditors treat infra fully managed but customer-tenant isolated)
- Confirm retention window for logs we promise vs. what we actually store in Datadog/S3 (alignment with retention policy doc).
- What level of evidence is acceptable for automated rollout tests (can unit/e2e pipeline runs + prod traces suffice)?

Control mapping (rough):
- CC1 (Control environment): org chart, security policy, HR background check process (people ops owns). Evidence: handbook, sample offer letter, background-check vendor receipts. Status: partial. Owner: Maya Singh.
- CC2 (Communication & Info): Slack + Confluence guidance for incidents, cross-team comms. Evidence: incident runbook v2, pager rota. Status: needs updates. Owner: Ryan Chen.
- CC3 (Risk assessment): high-level risk register + threat model for inference platform. Evidence: risk register (Confluence page), latest threat modeling session notes. Status: draft. Owner: Kiara Reyes.
- CC4 (Monitoring of logical access): IAM + SSO configs, admin role review cadence. Evidence: Okta admin group membership export, monthly review logs. Status: gap (no formal cadence documented). Owner: Oliver Park.
- CC5 (Change management): infra change approvals, release engineering PRs, canary rollout logs. Evidence: release calendar, sample RFCs, approval emails. Status: mostly good but need to capture approvals for hotfixes. Owner: Release Eng (TBD).
- CC6 (System operations): backups, DR runbooks, incident postmortems. Evidence: backup config (S3 lifecycle), recent DR test results — need a DR test in prod-sim. Status: insufficient recent DR test evidence. Owner: Eng-SRE.

Evidence inventory (what we have / need):
- Okta exports (have): partial — need historical snapshots for last 12 months.
- KMS access logs (have): Cloud KMS logs retained 90d; auditor wants 12mo — ask infra about extended retention + cost.
- Backup configs (have): S3 backups for certain datastores; need verification for others (e.g., ephemeral caches not required).
- Incident PMs (have): postmortems on major outages 2023-2024 exist; need a template to ensure consistent artifacts.
- Deployment approvals (partial): can pull GitHub PR approvals but need a formal approval matrix doc.

Immediate action items (priority order):
1) Confirm scope decision with audit partner (call scheduled w/ AuditFirm on 2024-11-09). Owner: Kiara.
2) Kick off evidence collection spreadsheet (one row per control/evidence, link to artifact). Owner: Maya to own sheet; Kiara populates initial rows.
3) Formalize admin role review cadence (doc one-time process + automate monthly export). Owner: Oliver.
4) DR test plan: schedule a tabletop + one small failover test for infra components by end of Q1 2025. Owner: Eng-SRE.
5) KMS retention ask: run cost estimate if we request 12mo logs (Infra + Finance). Owner: Ryan.

Notes to self: 
- Keep docs lightweight for now. Auditors prefer evidence that demonstrates consistent process over perfectly formatted artifacts.
- Capture screenshots where export pulls are manual (ex: Okta membership). Mark in sheet whether evidence is automated or manual snapshot.
- For Dedicated customers, prepare a template letter describing boundary of Redwood responsibility vs customer responsibility (legal to review).

Possible short-term wins (to get to "reasonably ready"):
- Produce a 12-month admin group membership CSV (manual exports + archive) — shows review activity.
- Create a simple release approval checklist template and enforce on all hotfix PRs for next 3 months.
- Run an internal DR tabletop and record decisions as evidence.

Risks / blockers:
- Some logs live in third-party tools with retention limits (Datadog). Might need to export and store in S3 for 12mo retention — budget impact.
- Coordination across multiple teams (release, SRE, infra, legal) — need a RACI in the sheet.

Next meeting notes (to prep):
- 2024-11-07 sync: bring control mapping skeleton + evidence inventory draft. Ask: who can provide Okta exports, KMS logs, backup configs?
- Bring specific asks (format & sample files) so engineers can produce artifacts quickly.

TODO (short checklist):
- [ ] Create evidence spreadsheet (link it to Confluence page) — Maya/Kiara
- [ ] Draft scope letter for auditor — Kiara + Legal
- [ ] Admin group monthly export script (POC) — Oliver
- [ ] DR tabletop schedule + invite list — Eng-SRE
- [ ] Cost estimate for 12mo KMS/Datadog retention — Ryan + Finance

End of scratchpad.

(If I get time: port mapping into the Confluence control matrix template and drop links to actual artifacts.)
